forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: East Midlands Combined County Authority forecasts £0.80m underspend on 2026/27 day-to-day budget
news_drafts.lead:
The East Midlands Combined County Authority, a body run by several councils together for transport and economic growth, forecasts that it will spend £0.80m less than its revised budget for day-to-day running costs (revenue spending) in 2026/27. Its first-quarter budget monitoring report (the in-year check of spending against budget) says: "This shows a forecast underspend of £0.80m, against the 2026/27 revised budget." The board considered the report at its meeting on 12 October.

The paper attributes the underspend mainly to surplus treasury interest, staffing underspends and reduced Land & Housing due diligence spend. It gives £2.0m of additional investment income. On staffing, the employer pension contribution rate fell from 16.3% to 13.2%, which the paper values at £0.58m. It also reports £0.30m of staffing underspends at the first quarter and cites vacant posts.

The forecast follows the transfer of £3.3m of underspends from one of the authority's portfolios into its corporate contingency, money held for unforeseen costs. The paper says the underspends are offset by the need to fund in-year budget pressures.

findings.committee: East Midlands Combined County Authority Board
findings.paper_title: Item 11 - Quarter 1 2026-27 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring
findings.headline: Q1 is the first monitoring cycle after the Technology One finance system went live in August 2026, and the paper expects further capital forecast refinement before Q2.
findings.detail: The paper says the capital programme will be reviewed on a regular basis and that refinement of capital forecasts is anticipated ahead of Quarter 2.
findings.matters: Councils migrating finance systems will be interested in whether forecasts are stable in the first monitoring cycle after go-live.
findings.quote: As this is the first monitoring cycle following the implementation of the new Technology One Finance System in August 2026

findings.committee: East Midlands Combined County Authority Board
findings.paper_title: Item 11 - Quarter 1 2026-27 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring
findings.headline: The Board is asked to approve consolidating the Development reserve into the Organisational Development and Capacity reserve, transferring a balance of £1.26m.
findings.detail: The paper describes the two earmarked reserves as serving similar purposes and proposes merging them under a single designation.
findings.matters: A reader watching reserve rationalisation will see how a council is reducing the number of earmarked balances.
findings.quote: The balance of £1.26m to be transferred from Development into the newly designated Organisational Development and Capacity.

findings.committee: East Midlands Combined County Authority Board
findings.paper_title: Item 11 - Quarter 1 2026-27 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring
findings.headline: EMCCA expects £1.4m of additional Local Authority Bus Grant from the Department for Transport in October 2026, proposed for transfer to the Transport reserve.
findings.detail: The grant is part of a wider government package announced alongside a £2 single bus fare cap across England in 2027. The paper says it is expected through the Quarter 3 Local Transport Consolidated Funding payment and is proposed to mitigate transport budget pressures.
findings.matters: Other councils managing bus networks will want to see how new DfT bus funding is being allocated against operating cost pressures.
findings.figures: £1.4m additional LABG revenue funding; £1.4m contribution to Transport reserves; £2 single bus fare cap (2027)
findings.quote: £1.4m of additional revenue funding through the Local Authority Bus Grant (LABG) from the Department for Transport.

findings.committee: East Midlands Combined County Authority Board
findings.paper_title: Item 11 - Quarter 1 2026-27 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring
findings.headline: Treasury management projects £6.5m of investment interest for 2026/27 against a £4.5m budget, an overachievement of £2.0m.
findings.detail: Q1 interest income was £1.85m. Rates ranged from 3.86% to 3.92% in money market funds, 4.35% with local authorities, 3.51% in call accounts and 1.41% with the bank. Section 3.7 separately reports a £2.3m investment income overachievement.
findings.matters: Surplus cash returning above budget is funding the revenue position, and the paper shows its contribution to the Q1 underspend.
findings.figures: £1.85m Q1 interest income; £4.5m approved 2026/27 budget; £6.5m projected year-end income; £2.0m projected overachievement; £2.3m forecast overachievement (section 3.7); 3.86%-3.92% money market fund rates; 4.35% local authority rate; 3.51% call account; 1.41% bank
findings.quote: the current year end projection is £6.5m, representing a projected overachievement of £2.0m against budget.

findings.committee: East Midlands Combined County Authority Board
findings.paper_title: Item 11 - Quarter 1 2026-27 Revenue and Capital Budget Monitoring
findings.headline: The Q1 capital programme is forecast at £251.4m against a revised budget of £254.2m, a £2.8m underspend attributed to reprofiling.
findings.detail: The paper says the variance is mainly reprofiling across a small number of schemes rather than a reduction in approved programme activity. Named variances include Creating Capacity for Post-16 Mainstream Education (£0.9m), Organisational Development (£0.8m, from reclassifying the Finance system from capital to revenue) and Angel Investment Fund (£0.7m).
findings.matters: Finance officers at other councils will recognise the reprofiling pattern from the revised budget of £289.6m reduced to £254.2m, and the reclassification of a finance system from capital to revenue.
findings.figures: £251.4m forecast capital expenditure; £254.2m revised capital budget; £2.8m forecast underspend; £289.6m original capital budget; £0.9m Post-16 Education underspend; £0.8m Organisational Development underspend; £0.7m Angel Investment Fund underspend
findings.quote: resulting in a forecast underspend of £2.8m
